title: Always useful
body:
There are so many ways to make use of this app! I love that I can set so many different kinds of goals and how I can track my progress! - From exercise routines to skill practice, to prioritising time for myself or time spent working with my kids HW or skill development. I can track application to chores or supporting health. 
I can choose time lengths to discipline myself to a task, or multiple counts of a task per day/week/month etc.
I can adjust how many times per day in how many days per week. I can choose which days in a week I specifically want to complete a task. 
It pings you with positive encouragement for achieving goals, you can choose from a vast variety of colour combinations to personalise it (including allowing the background to change at random or using light/dark mode) and you can archive goals you made, but don’t want to delete them (insteadsuspend them for a time).

I even love the different symbols you can choose from to match each of your tasks - making it easier to find the one you want to check off.
Also, best addition I found is when it started syncing to my Apple Watch! *I can check off items without even opening my phone.

If you like checklists, setting or tracking history of any goals or find you are really busy— this app will make life easier. (The calendar in the app even allows you to open it and fix any errors you entered or if you forgot to check off a previous day.)

*I just recommend taking the time to explore its options and try a couple of ways to count your goals. (Sometimes I found that one way of using the app was not as helpful as another, but I can always edit it.)

It’s looks great, works exactly as it should and negative habits are a wonderful feature. The only two things I would change is an optional ‘advance’ setting providing more in-depth graphical information, however, I am not even sure If I would ever use it. Also, would be nice if a habit (based on certain criteria) would ‘talk’ to you (with a speech bubble or something) and spur you on to rebuild a large habit streak, since if you break a big streak one could benefit from some encouragement. Would love to see this feature!

But I soon just thought what the hell and bought it anyway, and I’m so glad that I did. It’s really such a simple concept, you just add the tasks that you want to do, the app reminds you to do it or else you lose your streak. I’ve read some people on here just calling it a To Do list and that it’s not worth the money, but I’ve always wanted to journal but have quit just a few days after starting. But for the past 3 weeks that I’ve had this app I have journaled everyday. Just a regular To Do list app wouldn’t motivate me to journal daily, but this one does for fear of losing the streak I’ve worked hard to maintain. Other things I’ve been making sure I complete everyday include taking my vitamins, eating at least one fruit or vegetable, reading for 10 minutes, taking my dog for a walk - all of which I struggle to do regularly, let alone consecutively everyday for almost a month. 

So don’t worry about the money and just get the app, you’ll thank yourself when you’ve got all these good habits and you feel like you’re getting your life on track.

Streaks is really great for completing tasks, keeping up hobbies and just general motivation. I'm a big fan of the overall design, icons and support for iMessage stickers the Apple Watch.

My only major gripe is with sync performance on Apple Watch. I use a first-generation Apple Watch Sport running watchOS 3, with Streaks as a complication and in the dock for better memory/performance. Whilst other native and third-party apps in the dock are reliable and quick to update data, the Streaks complication hardly ever lights up the appropriate dots in sync with tasks marked as completed on my iPhone. This continues even after attempting reinstallation of the app on both devices.

Better performance on slightly older Watch hardware would earn a five-star review. :)

title: Nice balance between simplicity and utility
body:
I've tried both Streaks and its nearest competitor Productive, and Streaks manages to be easier to actually maintain. Productive is feature-packed, which means you tend to overload it with too many habits that you quickly fall behind on.

By contrast, Streaks has no time-of-day habits, and limits you to six habits total. This is definitely a selling point, since it forces you to think about what's actually important to you rather than trying to hold yourself to an impossible standard.

Streaks also has some nice HealthKit-powered smarts built in: reducing the busy-work of habits by automatically logging where possible certainly helps with actually maintaining a habit of using the app.

It's also the second app I use with an actually useful Apple Watch complication!
